## Physical scenario

In the reaction \( \text{K}^- + \text{p} \rightarrow \Lambda^0 + \pi^0 \), a charged K meson (mass \( 493.7 \text{ MeV}/c^2 \)) collides with a proton (\( 938.3 \text{ MeV}/c^2 \)) at rest, producing a lambda particle (\( 1115.7 \text{ MeV}/c^2 \)) and a neutral pi meson (\( 135.0 \text{ MeV}/c^2 \)), as represented in figure. The initial kinetic energy of the K meson is \( 152.4 \text{ MeV} \). After the interaction, the pi meson has a kinetic energy of \( 254.8 \text{ MeV} \).

## Question

Find the kinetic energy of the lambda.

## Answer choices

- A: A: \( 65.6 \text{ MeV} \)

- B: B: \( 90.4 \text{ MeV} \)

- C: C: \( 33.1 \text{ MeV} \)

- D: D: \( 78.9 \text{ MeV} \)

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image consists of two panels labeled (a) and (b), each depicting a physics diagram with particles and coordinate axes.

**Panel (a):**
- It shows two particles on a 2D coordinate system with axes labeled \(x\) and \(y\).
- A particle labeled \(K^-\) is moving along the negative x-axis towards a stationary particle labeled \(p\).
- There is an arrow indicating the direction of motion.

**Panel (b):**
- It depicts another scene on a 2D coordinate system with axes \(x\) and \(y\).
- Two particles are shown: \(\pi^0\) and \(\Lambda^0\).
- The particle \(\pi^0\) is moving at an angle \(\theta\) from the y-axis, depicted by an arrow.
- The particle \(\Lambda^0\) is depicted in motion at an angle \(\phi\) from the x-axis, shown by another arrow.
- The angles \(\theta\) and \(\phi\) are marked with curved arrows.

Both panels seem to illustrate some interaction or decay process involving particles with labeled directions.
